title: From Speech Tokens to Stolen Voices: Attacker-Chosen-Text Speaker Impersonation via Representation Inversion
abstract: arXiv:2610.34688v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Speech interaction systems have gradually evolved from traditional cascaded systems that use text as intermediate information to end-to-end speech language models that directly process speech representations. In some applications, the speech frontend runs on the user's device and sends speech representations to a remote server for inference, while the original audio remains local. However, these representations may still contain speaker identity information. If an attacker obtains them, it may use this information to imitate the user's voice, threatening their voice privacy. translated_title: 从语音标记到被盗声音：通过表示反演实现攻击者指定文本的说话人模仿
translated_abstract: 语音交互系统已经逐渐从以文本作为中间信息的传统级联系统，演变为直接处理语音表示的端到端语音语言模型。在某些应用中，语音前端运行在用户的设备上，并将语音表示发送到远程服务器进行推理，而原始音频则保留在本地。然而，这些表示可能仍包含说话人的身份信息。如果攻击者获取了这些表示，就可能利用其中的信息模仿用户的声音，从而威胁其语音隐私。为了研究这一风险，我们提出了STIA（语音标记反演攻击），该攻击仅利用一段泄露的短语音表示，在无需访问原始音频或其转录文本的情况下，生成攻击者指定文本的受害者声音语音。具体而言，STIA将离散、连续或混合的语音表示转换为条件序列，并训练……（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 本文提出语音标记反演攻击STIA，仅凭一段泄露的语音表示即可生成攻击者指定文本的受害者声音，揭示了即使原始音频不出本地设备，语音表示仍会泄露说话人身份的隐私风险。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes STIA, a Speech Token Inversion Attack that generates speech in a victim's voice with attacker-specified text from a single short leaked speech representation, revealing that speech representations can leak speaker identity even when the original audio never leaves the device.
